This suit for perpetual injunction is filed by the plaintiff for restraining infringement of trade mark/copyright, confusion, dilution, passing off, delivery up, rendition of accounts along with damages to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/- etc. against the defendant.
2. Brief facts:-

As per plaintiff, who is claiming itself to be a proprietorship concern having its office at 619/8, NOVA House, Chattarpur, New Delhi and the present suit was filed by one Sh. Mahesh Gupta, proprietor who was stated to be duly authorized on behalf the Plaintiff company to sign,
verify and file the present suit as he was fully aware of the facts of the present case.

It was stated that Plaintiff including its predecessors, licensees, permitted users, associates and affiliates, was a well known manufacturer and trader in Tea, Elachi, and was covered under class 30 of the Trade Marks Act, 1999, and its products and services were being marketed under the Trademark 'Nova' which had been in the market for decades.

sentences.text: Plaintiff was stated to have been the prior adopter, true owner and lawful proprietor of the trademark NOVA for Tea, Elachi and registered under the Trade Marks Act, 1999, and the said trademark was already registered in favour of the Plaintiff vide trade mark application no. 1592200 dated 20.08.2007, with the user date of 01.08.1992.

The aforesaid trademark had been renewed for a further period of 10 years, w.e.f. 20.08.2017 and valid till 20.08.2027, vide renewal certificate no.
RLC/280036 dated 24.03.2017 and had already established business on a large scale and had also obtained Sale Tax Certificate, GST Certificate and was regularly filing Income Tax Return.

Plaintiff was also stated to be the owner of NOVA (label) and had filed application for its art work and had filed TM- C vide receipt no. 2229218 dated 28.05.2019, for copyright, NOC of which was pending before the Trade Mark Registry.

Plaintiff had created a unique logo of its products under the name and style of "Surya Marketing Co." and its registered Trade Mark was "NOVA", hence, they had mentioned SMC along with brand NOVA on its packing to distinguish its products from other manufacturers.

It was stated that Plaintiff had also obtained the registration certificate under Food and Safety Standard Act, 2006 vide license No. 13314008000306 dated 25.11.2014 under the name and style of "SURYA MARKETING CO.", which was still valid.
The aforementioned trade mark had been registered under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 since the year 2001.

It was stated that Plaintiff's Trademark had become distinctive and widely recognized due to long term use and was highly demanded in the market on account of the high standard quality and during the past many years, Plaintiff had established large and extensive sale/service of its goods under the impugned trademark throughout the country.

It was averred that Plaintiff had been continuously using its trade mark in relation to goods and business and had built up a great reputation and enviable goodwill thereunder and had also acquired proprietary rights therein.

It was stated further that plaintiff had spent huge amount on the publicity and advertisement of the aforementioned goods, which helped the Plaintiff in increasing its annual trunover in millions of rupees.
3.

It was averred that Defendants had adopted and conceived the trade mark SMC NOVA in relation to its products like Coffee, Tea, Cocoa, Sugar, Rice, Tapioca, Sago, Artifical coffee, flour and preparations made from cereals, bread, pastry and confectionery, ices, honey, treacle, yeast, baking powder, salt, mustard, vinegar, sauces, (condiments), spices, ice thereof and had been passing off its aforesaid products of inferior and sub standard quality as compared to goods of the Plaintiff malafidely and dishonestly with the ulterior object of trading upon the goodwill and reputation of the Plaintiff and had been earning profit by such illegal means.
Products of the Plaintiff were stated to have gained good reputation due to distinguishable features in terms of set up shape, size, layout marking and packaging.

Plaintiff had advertised its products under the aforesaid trademark for the past twenty seven years and had become very famous Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92795922/
2 amongst the buyers.

sentences.text: It was stated that defendant had been fraudulently selling the TEA, ELACHI through its vending outlets in DELHI/ NCR DELHI under the Trademark SMC NOVA, and misleading the public into believing that these products were that of plaintiff and thereby infringing the Plaintiff's trademark.
Defendant had been passing off its goods as those of plaintiff's goods and was getting the benefits from the goodwill and reputation of plaintiff.

It was averred further that defendant's marketing and advertising of its products were deceiving and misleading the public at large as buyers believed that those products were of the Plaintiff due to which Plaintiff had suffered significant losses and injury.
It was stated that the loss of money or injury sustained or likely to be sustained by the Plaintiff due to erroneous actions and conduct of defendant could not be calculated in terms of money.

It was stated that the Plaintiff had built an unquestionable goodwill and unsullied reputation across the country with the Trademark NOVA, which was being widely recognized even amongst illiterate because of its extensive publicity.

The reckless use of the trade mark SMC NOVA by the defendant for its products like coffee, tea, flour and preparations made from cereals and other related items,
could easily deceive consumers into thinking that the defendant's products originated from Plaintiff.

The conduct of the defendant was likely to damage the goodwill, reputation and business of the Plaintiff by selling inferior quality of products and defendant had been earning huge profits by such illegal and unlawful manners.

Defendant's office was stated to have been situated within a distance of 10 km from the office of Plaintiff, which created confusion in the minds of buyers and local marketers and caused them to believe that it was an extension/ division/ associate franchisee of the Plaintiff.
By using aforementioned trademark of the Plaintiff, defendant would have caused injury not only to the goodwill and reputation of the Plaintiff, but also deceive the unwary consumers at large.

4. The cause of action was stated to have arisen firstly on 24.04.2009, when the plaintiff noticed the goods bearing the trademark SMC NOVA identical/similar to the Plaintiff's said trademark and cause of action again arose when Plaintiff had come to know about the illegal and unlawful trade activities of the defendant.
The cause of action was stated to be still continuing and subsisting in favor of the Plaintiff and against the Defendant.
5. Since the registered office of plaintiff company was in Delhi and Plaintiff was also working for gain in Delhi.

Since Defendant was also selling its products within the jurisdiction of this court,
hence this court was stated to have territorial jurisdiction to try and decide the present suit.

6. In the light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the plaintiff had prayed for passing of a decree in favour of Plaintiff and against the defendant detailed as hereunder:-

ii) For perpetual injuction restraining the Defendant, their servants and agents from infringing the copyright in the trade mark SMC NOVA.

Upon service of notice, the defendant also appeared to contest the case of plaintiff on its merits and filed his written statement on record, wherein he had taken a preliminary objection that plaintiff was guilty of concealment of material facts as well as for not approaching the court with clean hands.
No cause of action was stated to have arisen in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant.
8. On merits it was stated that defendant had purchased the name 'NOVA' on 25.08.2020 as a word for class 30 from the manufacturer and traders which had already been registered since 22.09.2000.
Defendant got it registered in its own name on 15.10.2020.
Except for the paras which were either specifically admitted or essentially or purely constituted a matter of record, rest others were denied by it as wrong and incorrect.

17. In view of aforesaid arguments and submissions of the parties as well as evidence appearing on record, my issue wise findings are as under:
1.
Whether Plaintiff is the prior user and owner of the trademark 'NOVA' in India?
OPP The onus to prove this issue was upon the plaintiff.
From the evidence lead on record as discussed in detail in the preceding paras, it has been duly established that Plaintiff has been the prior user of trademark NOVA.
Hence, issue is accordingly answered in affirmative and decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant.

sentences.text: Whether by using the trademark 'NOVA/SMC NOVA/SMC NOVA ESTATE' defendant has infringed the registered trademark NOVA of the Plaintiff?

OPP Onus to prove this issue was also upon the plaintiff and though present defendant in its written statement had claimed to have purchased the said trademark from its erstwhile owners, however, neither the name of previous owner has been disclosed nor he has been examined as a witness in this case to support the case of the defendant.

As already pleaded by the Plaintiff in the suit, he had been using the aforesaid trademark since 01.08.1992 and got the same registered on 20.08.2007, whereas, as per the defendant, he had purchased the said trademark on 25.08.2020, which was registered on 22.09.2000 and the registration got transferred in favour of defendant on 15.10.2020.
Since the plea of plaintiff being user of the trademark since 01.08.1992 has remained unrebutted and unchallenged.
Therefore, present issue is also answered in affirmative and in favour of the Plaintiff and against the defendant.
3. Whether defendant is passing of the goods of the Plaintiff?
OPP 4. Whether use of the similar/identical trade-dress and packaging by the defendant has resulted in infringement and passing off the copyright in the packaging of the Plaintiff?
OPP Onus to prove these issues was again upon the plaintiff.

As held in my findings in respect of issues no. 1 and 2 above, I have no hesitation in holding that from the unrebutted and unchallenged testimony of PW1,
it has been clearly established that defendant is passing off the goods of the Plaintiff by using similar/ identical trade dress and packaging, which has amounted to an infringment and passing off the copyright in the packaging of Plaintiff, so as to give an impression to the customers at large that they are buying the goods of the Plaintiff instead of those being of defendant.
Hence, both the aforesaid issues are answered in affirmative and are decided in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant.
5. Whether Plaintiff is entitled to damages of Rs. Five Lakhs as claimed?

OPP Since the Plaintiff's trademark has been infringed by the defendant as has been clearly established on record, hence, I have no hesitation in holding that the Plaintiff is also entitled to the damages and keeping in view the age of the matter, which is almost 5 years old now, the damages of Rs. 5,00,000/- as claimed by the Plaintiff from the defendant do not appear to be that on a much higher side.

A bare perusal of packaging material of both the parties makes it amply clear that colour combination as well as font and entire packaging of the defendant is almost similar and identical to that of the plaintiff.

Therefore, this issue is also answered in affirmative and is decided in favour of the Plaintiff and against the defendant holding the Plaintiff to be entitled to claim damages to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/- and same are awarded accordingly along with pendentelite and future interest @ 8% p.a.
6.
Relief and costs 18.

In view of my findings given to all the issues above, the suit of the Plaintiff is decreed with costs and defendant is hereby also restrained permanently from using any such packaging material, which is similar or identical to that of the packaging material of the Plaintiff.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This suit for perpetual injunction is filed by the plaintiff for restraining infringement of trade mark/copyright, confusion, dilution, passing off, delivery up, rendition of accounts along with damages to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/- etc. against the defendant.
It was stated that Plaintiff including its predecessors, licensees, permitted users, associates and affiliates, was a well known manufacturer and trader in Tea, Elachi, and was covered under class 30 of the Trade Marks Act, 1999, and its products and services were being marketed under the Trademark 'Nova' which had been in the market for decades.
Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92795922/
1
Plaintiff was also stated to be the owner of NOVA (label) and had filed application for its art work and had filed TM- C vide receipt no. 2229218 dated 28.05.2019, for copyright, NOC of which was pending before the Trade Mark Registry.
The aforementioned trade mark had been registered under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 since the year 2001.
6. In the light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the plaintiff had prayed for passing of a decree in favour of Plaintiff and against the defendant detailed as hereunder:-
Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92795922/
3 1) For perpetual injunction, restraining the defendant, their servants, agents,
representative, dealers and all other persons on their behalf from passing off their said products of tea, Elachi thereof under the offending trade mark SMC NOVA or under any other identical with and/ or deceptively Similar trade mark as that of the plaintiff well known and well Routed trade mark NOVA in relation to their products of tea, Elachi.
ii) For perpetual injuction restraining the Defendant, their servants and agents from infringing the copyright in the trade mark SMC NOVA.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since PW-1 Arun Gupta was examined in chief and his cross-examination was deferred on 11.10.2022.
After that, several opportunities were granted to and availed by the defendant during the intervening period of more than one and half years but defendant had not bothered to cross-examine the PW1.
Since the establishment of commercial courts was done with a view to expedite the disposal of commercial matters, however, this case is a glaring example of abuse of process by the parties.
13. Hence, defendant's right to cross-examine the PW-1 stood closed and Plaintiff's evidence was also closed.
14. Defendant had not lead any evidence in his defence.
15. Hence, Defendant's evidence was also closed.
Whether Plaintiff is the prior user and owner of the trademark 'NOVA' in India?
Hence, issue is accordingly answered in affirmative and decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant.
Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92795922/
9 2.
Whether by using the trademark 'NOVA/SMC NOVA/SMC NOVA ESTATE' defendant has infringed the registered trademark NOVA of the Plaintiff?
OPP Onus to prove this issue was also upon the plaintiff and though present defendant in its written statement had claimed to have purchased the said trademark from its erstwhile owners, however, neither the name of previous owner has been disclosed nor he has been examined as a witness in this case to support the case of the defendant.
As already pleaded by the Plaintiff in the suit, he had been using the aforesaid trademark since 01.08.1992 and got the same registered on 20.08.2007, whereas, as per the defendant, he had purchased the said trademark on 25.08.2020, which was registered on 22.09.2000 and the registration got transferred in favour of defendant on 15.10.2020.
Since the plea of plaintiff being user of the trademark since 01.08.1992 has remained unrebutted and unchallenged.
As held in my findings in respect of issues no. 1 and 2 above, I have no hesitation in holding that from the unrebutted and unchallenged testimony of PW1,
it has been clearly established that defendant is passing off the goods of the Plaintiff by using similar/ identical trade dress and packaging, which has amounted to an infringment and passing off the copyright in the packaging of Plaintiff, so as to give an impression to the customers at large that they are buying the goods of the Plaintiff instead of those being of defendant.
Hence, both the aforesaid issues are answered in affirmative and are decided in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant.
OPP Since the Plaintiff's trademark has been infringed by the defendant as has been clearly established on record, hence, I have no hesitation in holding that the Plaintiff is also entitled to the damages and keeping in view the age of the matter, which is almost 5 years old now, the damages of Rs. 5,00,000/- as claimed by the Plaintiff from the defendant do not appear to be that on a much higher side.
A bare perusal of packaging material of both the parties makes it amply clear that colour combination as well as font and entire packaging of the defendant is almost similar and identical to that of the plaintiff.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, this issue is also answered in affirmative and is decided in favour of the Plaintiff and against the defendant holding the Plaintiff to be entitled to claim damages to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/- and same are awarded accordingly along with pendentelite and future interest @ 8% p.a.
6.
Relief and costs 18.
In view of my findings given to all the issues above, the suit of the Plaintiff is decreed with costs and defendant is hereby also restrained permanently from using any such packaging material, which is similar or identical to that of the packaging material of the Plaintiff.
